stem.en: Riya studies a living permanent cell that stores food in the stem of a mango tree. Which statement about this cell is most likely correct?

text.en: In the plant body it normally does not divide again, but under special conditions it can start dividing.
It divides as quickly as a meristem cell does, because every living cell in a plant keeps on dividing all the time.

feedback.en: Only meristem cells divide continuously and rapidly. Permanent cells have lost the ability to divide in the normal plant body.

text.en: It can never divide again under any conditions, because it is a permanent cell.

feedback.en: "Never" goes too far. Some living permanent cells can start dividing again under special conditions.

text.en: It turns back into a meristem cell as soon as it is moved close to a root tip.

feedback.en: Moving a cell does not undo differentiation. Its structure and function stay the same in its new place.

explanation.en: A permanent cell has lost the ability to divide, so in the normal plant body it does not divide again. This is not true of every cell for ever: some living permanent cells, such as food-storing cells, can start dividing again under special conditions.

hints.en: Is the cell living or dead? Does that matter?
Look for the option that is not too strong in either direction.
